There are hints of persuasion (hospitalist 'wasn't eager to admit', pushing radiology) but the text does not show the participant actively negotiating or persuading in detail, so evidence is too thin for a confident secondary label.

ambiguities: A2.5 vs A2.6: The Wells score recalculation could be framed as either diagnostic conceptualisation (applying/refining a model) or as creative problem resolution (adapting to a non-routine combination of findings). A3.4 vs B2 Teamwork: Coordinating with resident/nurse/radiology/hospitalist could be classified as either managing/coordinating (content) or simply collaborative teamwork (method). Both are recorded, with A3.4 as content evidence and teamwork rated separately under methods.

task_anchors.task_description: Managing multiple acute patients simultaneously under bed/boarding pressure while being brought a new chest pain case by a resident
Interpreting physical exam finding (chest wall tenderness) alongside history (flight, calf ache) to weigh competing explanations
Integrating new calf finding and D-dimer result into a formal risk score with the resident to determine need for imaging
Coordinating with radiology to prioritize CTPA within an existing queue under time pressure
Retrieving and evaluating a colleague's prior documented decision to assess reasoning quality independent of outcome
Weighing an eventful but clinically stable visit against bed pressure and patient preference to decide discharge vs admission
